**Customer feedback trends regarding citation reliability shifted from a critical, widespread issue in Q1 2026 to a significantly improved but not fully resolved state in Q2 2026.**

**Q1 2026 (Deterioration):** Citation reliability was the single most prominent complaint during the quarter [NL-010-S01]. An audit of 210 accuracy-related tickets showed a clear breakdown: Incorrect File Links (42%), Missing Page Numbers (28%), Empty Citations (18%), and Broken Links (12%) [NL-010-S05]. These issues had severe operational consequences, causing BrightPath Healthcare to pause their clinical pilot and Northstar Financial to lose confidence in the platform [NL-010-S05].

**Q2 2026 (Improvement):** The general sentiment improved dramatically after the April 2026 product release. Support tickets for citation accuracy declined steadily throughout Q2, with monthly counts dropping from 88 in March to 42 in April, 31 in May, and 24 in June [NL-011-S05]. The April fix successfully resolved critical complaints, reducing complaints regarding incorrect or missing citations significantly, and restoring client confidence—BrightPath Healthcare restarted its clinical pilot after verifying correct page-level citations [NL-011-S03]. The overall Net Promoter Score (NPS) rose to 44 (up from 41 in Q1) [NL-011-S01].

**Remaining Issues (Q2):** Citation tickets did not drop to zero. The remaining tickets are almost entirely linked to scanned, image-only PDFs, where the platform struggles to establish citation anchors [NL-011-S05]. Additionally, there is a minor lag in citation indexing during peak business hours [NL-011-S05]. Advanced OCR capabilities remain a significant pain point, especially for healthcare and manufacturing customers with legacy policy manuals [NL-016-S04].
